citation: 12 CFR Part 53 (OCC); 12 CFR 225 Subpart N (FRB); 12 CFR 304 Subpart C (FDIC)
summary: Banking organizations notify regulator of 'notification incidents' within 36 hours; bank service providers notify bank customers of 4+ hour material disruptions.
applies_to: Banking organizations (national banks, FSAs, state banks, BHCs, etc.) and bank service providers.

short_name: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B (OCC); 12 CFR 208 App. D-2 & 225 App. F (FRB); 12 CFR 364 App. B (FDIC)
summary: Board-approved information security program: risk assessment, access controls, encryption, monitoring, service provider oversight, incident response and customer notice guidance, annual board report.
applies_to: National banks, federal savings associations, state member/nonmember banks, bank holding companies.
size_thresholds: No size exemption; program must be appropriate to size and complexity.

summary: Federally insured credit unions report reportable cyber incidents to NCUA within 72 hours.
SCI entities must maintain policies for capacity, integrity, resiliency, availability and security of SCI systems, BC/DR, testing, annual SCI review, and report SCI events.
applies_to: SCI entities: SCI SROs (exchanges, registered clearing agencies, FINRA, MSRB), SCI ATSs, plan processors, exempt clearing agencies subject to ARP, SCI competing consolidators.
size_thresholds: Volume-based for ATSs: during 4 of prior 6 months, NMS stocks >= 5% in any single stock AND >= 0.25% of all NMS stock ADDV, or >= 1% of all NMS stock ADDV; non-NMS equities >= 5% ADDV; 6-month grace period after first meeting threshold.

summary: CISO, risk-based cybersecurity program and policies, annual risk assessment, pen testing, MFA, asset inventory, access privilege reviews, encryption, IR/BCDR plans, third-party policy, annual certification/acknowledgment, board oversight.
applies_to: Entities licensed/registered/chartered under NY Banking, Insurance or Financial Services Law (banks, insurers, agents/brokers, money transmitters, mortgage cos., virtual currency).
size_thresholds: Limited exemption (500.19(a)): < 20 employees and independent contractors (incl. affiliates); OR < $7,500,000 gross annual revenue in each of last 3 fiscal years from NY operations; OR < $15,000,000 year-end total assets (incl. affiliates) -> exempt from 500.4, 500.5, 500.6, 500.8, 500.10, portions of 500.14, 500.15 and 500.16. 'Class A company' = >= $20M NY revenue and (> 2,000 employees or > $1B gross revenue) in each of last 2 fiscal years -> extra duties (independent audit, EDR, PAM, password controls).
status: Second Amendment effective Nov 1, 2023. Phased: 500.17 notices Dec 1, 2023; most new reqs Apr 29, 2024; 500.4/500.15/500.16/500.19(a) Nov 1, 2024; 500.5(a)(2)/500.7/500.14(a)(2)/500.14(b) May 1, 2025; 500.12 (MFA) and 500.13(a) (asset inventory) Nov 1, 2025 - all now in force.

citation: 6 U.S.C. 681b; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (89 FR 23644, Apr 4, 2024)
summary: Will require covered critical infrastructure entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours.
applies_to: Covered entities in critical infrastructure sectors as defined in the final rule (scope still being refined).
size_thresholds: Proposed rule included size-based criteria tied to SBA small-business standards plus sector-based criteria; final scope TBD.
status: NOT YET IN EFFECT: no final rule published as of 2026-09-25. CISA held additional town halls (Feb and May 2026 notices) to refine scope and burden before a final rule. Statutory reporting duties apply only once the final rule is effective.
